newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's trade head talks tough on culture, Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Canada's trade head talks tough on culture, Cuba.

text.p: Canada's new trade minister, Sergio Marchi, said on Wednesday that Canada would stand up for its cultural policies and stay the course on Cuba.
"I believe in our cultural policy and I don't think we should take it on the chin from anybody," Marchi told reporters after being named to his post.
"We have great neighbors in the Americans, the best trading partners...I will work to stand up for ourselves and promote Canada.

Canada has recently had run-ins with the United States over its policies to promote the Canadian magazine industry and over new copyright legislation. The magazine dispute is being fought through the World Trade Organization.
As for Cuba, Marchi urged the United States to be more conciliatory.
"I hope that the United States plans to reconcile with us," Marchi said. "I think they're on the wrong side of the issue."

While the United States has imposed economic sanctions on Cuba and threatened to penalize companies from other countries that do business with the island, Canada has actively pursued trade and investment there.
Canada argues that Cuban human rights and democracy will improve through better diplomatic relations.

"I would hope that they come around to our position to see that isolationist policy helps no one," Marchi said. "It doesn't help Cuba, it doesn't scare Cuba, and it certainly doesn't help the United States."
Marchi said he would continue to encourage the growth of Canadian exports through trade missions and by encouraging small and medium-sized businesses to expand.
"I think I'm a bit of a nationalist and I'd like to stand up very strongly for our country, both economically as well as culturally, and not take on the chin from anyone."
But Marchi was not as adamant as his predecessor Art Eggleton in pursuing closer ties with South American free trade block Mercosur.

"I think personally we should allow Mercosur to develop," he said. "A number of those countries want to be part of NAFTA, so I see it as a bridge starting from opposite ends and meeting in the middle."
Eggleton has said frequently that Canada had been in talks with Mercosur in the hopes of growing closer to Mercosur and increasing Canada's exports and investment to Mercosur countries.
Mercosur groups Brazil, Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay. Chile and Bolivia are associate members.
